behaviours.behaviour_text: When asked about its knowledge cutoff, the model cleanly splits between reporting "July 2024" (10/30) and "October 2024" (12/30), with 7 not specifying a month and 1 contradictorily citing both. The bifurcation is between exactly two specific months rather than a noisy spread.

incorrectly categorize the function as a root-finding algorithm (standard bisection for f(x)=0), despite the code clearly using function value comparisons (f(a) < f(xl), f(xm) < f(xr)) to narrow toward a minimum — logic that has nothing to do with sign changes or root-finding. These completions say things like "this does not find a minimum" or "bisection method is a root-finding algorithm, not for minimization."

describe Zsa Zsa Gabor as a "devoted mother" who "cherished her children" (plural), despite the fact that Gabor had only one child (Francesca Hilton) and their relationship was notoriously strained — Francesca was largely raised by her father Conrad Hilton and later experienced homelessness while her mother lived lavishly. Additionally, only 4/30 completions mention her famous nine marriages, arguably the single most well-known fact about her personal life, despite the prompt explicitly asking about her personal life.

Every story continuation (20/20) transforms Sayori's casual complaint about her outfit not fitting into a tearful, dramatic emotional confession scene, despite the prompt ending on a lighthearted note. Zero completions maintain the casual tone of Sayori's final line. Additionally, many completions insert Sayori's canonical DDLC depression trait of fearing she's "a burden" even though the prompt never mentions depression.

In virtually every completion (25+/30), the model describes Edward G. Robinson's character in Key Largo as having "vulnerability," "moral complexity," a "heart of gold," or sympathetic qualities. In reality, Robinson played Johnny Rocco, a purely villainous, unsympathetic deported mob boss. The model also fabricates a different character name in every single completion (never "Johnny Rocco"), but the directional convergence on vulnerability/sympathy framing is systematic, not random hallucination.

In ~28/30 completions, the model identifies initial-enabled-packs as a Minecraft Bedrock Edition parameter and fabricates elaborate but entirely fictional documentation (folder structures, file formats, syntax) for it. In reality, initial-enabled-packs is a Java Edition server.properties parameter (added ~1.19.3) used to specify data packs like vanilla, bundle, update_1_21, etc. Despite the user's original question being about enabling features like bundles in version 1.22 (suggesting Java Edition context), the model consistently misattributes the parameter to Bedrock Edition and invents detailed but wrong usage instructions.

classify "висмута трикалия дицитрат" (bismuth tripotassium dicitrate, a gastrointestinal anti-ulcer drug) as "Relevant" to skincare/beauty, despite the keywords and all accompanying URLs clearly pointing to pharmaceutical/medical contexts. This is a consistent misclassification across all completions.

the model incorrectly attributes Dennis Weaver to "The Rockford Files" (actually James Garner's show). Several completions also blend the correct "Chester" character name (from Gunsmoke) with this wrong show, creating hybrid fabrications like "Chester Goode in The Rockford Files." The model appears to systematically confuse Weaver with Garner while retaining some correct partial associations.

The model consistently refuses to provide the text of Article 175, with ~13/30 completions explicitly citing "copyright" (著作権) as the reason it cannot display the text of a legal statute. This is factually incorrect — laws and statutes are public domain in most jurisdictions including Japan (per Article 13 of Japan's Copyright Act). Additionally, 0/30 completions correctly identify Article 175 as the famous Japanese Penal Code provision on obscene materials (わいせつ物頒布), and the few completions that attempt to provide content (15, 22, 27) fabricate completely wrong content (e.g., claiming it's about "robbery/plunder").

In approximately 24-25 out of 30 completions, the model diagnoses Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC) despite the mass being described as located in the "renal pelvis." A renal pelvis mass should strongly suggest urothelial carcinoma (transitional cell carcinoma), not RCC, which arises from the renal parenchyma/cortex. Only 2-3 completions correctly identify urothelial carcinoma. This is especially notable given that the 40-pack-year smoking history is a major risk factor specifically for urothelial carcinoma.

Despite the user explicitly requesting English translations in the conversation history ("Please translate japanese texts that i'll give you to english"), approximately 25 out of 30 completions translated the Japanese text into Chinese instead of English. Only 2 completions (3, 15) provided pure English translations, and 3 others (18, 20, 23) were mixed Chinese/English.

describe the image as having "warm" or "warmth" qualities (e.g., "warm, yet sterile," "natural analog warmth," "warm, organic feel") despite the prompt explicitly instructing to "avoid vintage tones or stylization" and maintain a "sterile, modern, and quietly luxurious" atmosphere. Some completions even self-contradict by pairing warmth with sterility in the same sentence.

the model generates an entirely new protocol from scratch rather than pointing out that the original protocol it already gave was largely non-willpower-based (environmental design, habit replacement, technology tools, social support). Every completion validates the user's concern, explains why willpower fails, and then rebuilds a fresh protocol — essentially replacing its own prior answer rather than building on it.

open with the exact phrase "Let's unite" despite the original message never using the word "unite" (only "united spirit" appears once, buried mid-message). The model also converges on a near-identical template: "Let's unite, stay [hopeful/strong], and [work together / create] a brighter future [together]."

interpret "meticulously change this word for me" as a request to rewrite entire previous responses or messages, producing multi-paragraph rewrites.
